Office visits
Primary care visits cost $30 per visit, and the deductible does not apply. Specialist visits cost $65 per visit when you have a referral from your primary care provider on file before the appointment. items.answer: Full-time employees can enroll, change plans, or add dependents from November 2 through November 20, 2026.

sources.title: Corvane Workplace PPO - Who you can cover as a dependent
sources.text:
You can add eligible dependents to your Corvane Workplace PPO coverage when you first enroll, during your open enrollment window, or after a qualifying life event.

Eligible dependents
Your legal spouse or registered domestic partner is eligible. Children are eligible until the end of the month in which they turn 26, whether or not they live with you, are married, or are enrolled in school. A child over 26 remains eligible if the child cannot support themselves because of a physical or mental disability that began before age 26 and Corvane receives a disability certification from the child's physician.

Documents we ask for
When you add a dependent, Corvane may ask for a marriage certificate, domestic partnership registration, birth certificate, adoption decree, or court order. If the documents are not received within 45 days of the request, the dependent's coverage will be removed back to the date it began.

Who is not eligible
Parents, grandparents, siblings, and other relatives are not eligible unless a court has appointed you as their legal guardian.

sources.title: Corvane Mutual - Keeping your coverage after you leave your job
sources.text:
If you lose eligibility for the Corvane Workplace PPO because you leave your job, your hours are reduced, or you are no longer a dependent, you may be able to continue the same coverage for a limited time by paying the premium yourself.

How long continuation lasts
Continuation coverage generally lasts up to 18 months after a job loss or reduction in hours. Dependents who lose eligibility because of divorce or a child aging out of the plan can continue coverage for up to 36 months.

What it costs
You pay the full premium that your employer previously shared, plus a 2% administrative fee. Premiums are due on the first day of each month, with a 30-day grace period.

How to elect
Your employer will send an election notice within 44 days after your coverage ends. You have 60 days from the date of the notice to elect continuation coverage. If you elect it, coverage is restored back to the date your previous coverage ended, so there is no gap.

sources.title: Corvane Workplace PPO - Enrollment windows for the 2027 plan year
sources.text:
Corvane Mutual administers the Workplace PPO on behalf of participating employers. This page explains when employees can enroll in the plan or change their elections for the 2027 plan year.

Annual open enrollment
Full-time employees can enroll, change plans, or add dependents from November 2 through November 20, 2026. For enrollment purposes, full-time means regularly scheduled for 30 or more hours per week. Benefit-eligible part-time employees have a separate window that runs from October 12 through October 30, 2026, because their elections are reviewed by the employer's benefits office before they are sent to Corvane. Elections made in either window take effect on January 1, 2027.

New hires
Newly hired employees have 31 days from their first day of work to enroll. Coverage starts on the first day of the month after Corvane receives the enrollment form.

Changes during the year
Outside your open enrollment window, you can change elections only after a qualifying life event, such as marriage, the birth or adoption of a child, or the loss of other coverage. You must submit the change and supporting documents within 60 days of the event.

sources.text:
Pellagrine Virtual Care connects members with licensed clinicians by video or phone. Virtual visits are suited to minor illnesses, rashes, medication questions, and follow-up care that does not need a physical exam.

What you pay
Your cost for a virtual visit depends on your plan. Bronze 7000 members pay $0 per virtual visit from January 1 through June 30, 2026, after which the copay becomes $45 per virtual visit for the rest of the plan year. Silver 4000 members pay a $20 copay per virtual visit throughout the 2026 plan year. Gold 1500 members pay a $10 copay per virtual visit throughout the 2026 plan year. On every plan, the virtual visit copay applies whether or not you have met your deductible.

Therapy by video
Video sessions with an in-network therapist are billed as behavioral health office visits, not as virtual visits, and follow the behavioral health cost sharing in your plan summary.

When not to use virtual care
Virtual visits cannot be used for emergencies, for prescriptions of controlled substances, or for conditions that need same-day lab work. If the clinician decides you need to be seen in person, you will not be charged for the virtual visit.

sources.title: Pellagrine Health Partners - 2026 individual plans at a glance
sources.text:

Individual deductible of $7,000 and out-of-pocket maximum of $9,100. After the deductible, most services are covered at 40% coinsurance.

Gold 1500
Individual deductible of $1,500 and out-of-pocket maximum of $6,000. After the deductible, most services are covered at 15% coinsurance.

sources.title: Pellagrine Virtual Care - Getting ready for your first visit
sources.text:
You can join a Pellagrine Virtual Care visit from the Pellagrine mobile app or from a web browser on a computer with a camera and microphone.

Before your visit
Sign in with your member ID and date of birth, then confirm the phone number where the clinician can reach you if the video connection drops. Have a list of your current medications and any allergies ready. If the visit is for a child under 18, a parent or guardian must be present for the whole visit.

Connection tips
A connection of at least 2 megabits per second gives the best video quality. If your video freezes, the clinician will first try to reconnect and then call the phone number on file to finish the visit by voice.

After your visit
A visit summary appears in the app within one hour. If the clinician sends a prescription, it goes to the pharmacy you selected during sign-in. You can rate your clinician and leave comments from the visit summary screen.

sources.title: Silvermarsh Benefit Trust Standard Plan - Skilled nursing facility care
sources.text:
Skilled nursing facility (SNF) care is short-term care in a licensed facility for members who need daily nursing or rehabilitation after a hospital stay.

When SNF care is covered
The Standard Plan covers SNF care after an inpatient hospital stay of at least three consecutive days, when the member is admitted to the SNF within 30 days of discharge for the same condition. The SNF must be in the Silvermarsh network.

How much is covered
Coverage is limited to 100 days per benefit period. Days 1 through 20 are covered at no cost after the deductible. Days 21 through 100 are covered at 20% coinsurance. A benefit period ends when the member has gone 60 days in a row without inpatient hospital or SNF care.

What SNF coverage does not include
Private rooms, personal comfort items such as a television or telephone, and long-term residential care are not covered under the SNF benefit.

sources.title: Silvermarsh Benefit Trust Standard Plan - Home health care
sources.text:
Silvermarsh Benefit Trust covers certain care delivered in your home as an alternative to a hospital or skilled nursing stay. This section describes home health coverage under the Standard Plan for the 2026 plan year.

Home health aide visits
The Standard Plan covers home health aide visits when a physician certifies that the member is homebound. A member is considered homebound when leaving home requires considerable effort and the help of another person or a medical device. Without that certification, home health aide visits are not covered, even if a physician has ordered them.

Visit limits and cost sharing
Coverage is limited to 60 home health visits per plan year, combining aide, nursing, and therapy visits. Each visit is covered at 20% coinsurance after the deductible.

Care plan approval
The home health agency must submit a care plan, and Silvermarsh must approve it before the first visit. Silvermarsh reviews each approved care plan every 60 days.

Services that are not covered
Housekeeping, meal delivery, and round-the-clock custodial care at home are not covered.

sources.title: Silvermarsh Benefit Trust - Appealing a coverage decision
sources.text:
If Silvermarsh denies a claim or a request for prior approval, you have the right to ask us to look at the decision again. This is called an appeal.

First-level appeal
Send your appeal in writing within 180 days of the date on the denial letter. Include the claim or reference number, a short explanation of why you disagree, and any records from your doctor that support your request. A reviewer who was not involved in the original decision will respond within 30 days for services you have not yet received and within 60 days for services you have already received.

Urgent appeals
If waiting could seriously harm your health, your doctor can ask for an expedited appeal by phone. Silvermarsh decides expedited appeals within 72 hours.

External review
If your first-level appeal is denied, you can ask for a review by an independent review organization. Ask within four months of the final denial. The organization's decision is binding on Silvermarsh.

sources.text:

The Standard Plan covers SNF care after an inpatient hospital stay of at least three consecutive days, when the member is admitted to the SNF within 30 days of discharge for the same condition. The SNF must be in the Silvermarsh network.

How much is covered
Coverage is limited to 100 days per benefit period. Days 1 through 20 are covered at no cost after the deductible. Days 21 through 100 are covered at 20% coinsurance. A benefit period ends when the member has gone 60 days in a row without inpatient hospital or SNF care.

Private rooms, personal comfort items such as a television or telephone, and long-term residential care are not covered under the SNF benefit.

sources.text:

Housekeeping, meal delivery, and round-the-clock custodial care at home are not covered.

sources.text:

sources.title: Wrenhollow Care Cooperative - Help paying your premium
sources.text:
The Wrenhollow Member Assistance Fund lowers monthly premiums for individual and family plan members with limited household income. The fund is paid for by the cooperative and is separate from any government program.

Who qualifies
Households with income at or below 250% of the regional income benchmark published by Wrenhollow each October can apply. Members must live in the Wrenhollow service area and must not be eligible for an employer plan that meets Wrenhollow's affordability standard.

How much it pays
Assistance ranges from $40 to $310 per member per month, depending on household size and income. The amount is applied directly to your bill, so you pay only the remaining premium.

How to apply
Apply with the same form you use to enroll, or add an application later from your online account. You will need recent pay stubs or last year's tax return. Approved assistance starts with the next monthly bill and must be renewed every year.

sources.title: Wrenhollow Care Cooperative - Ending your coverage
sources.text:
You can end your Wrenhollow individual or family plan at any time. This page explains when coverage ends and what happens to premiums you have already paid.

How to cancel
Sign in to your online account and choose End Coverage, or call Member Services. You can cancel coverage for the whole household or for one member only.

When coverage ends
If you ask to end coverage on a date at least 14 days in the future, coverage ends on that date. If you ask with less notice, coverage ends 14 days after your request, unless you are ending coverage because you enrolled in other health coverage, in which case it can end the day before the new coverage starts.

Premium refunds
If you paid premiums for any month after your coverage ends, Wrenhollow refunds the overpayment to your original payment method within 30 days. Partial months are refunded on a daily basis.

If a member dies
Coverage ends on the date of death, and any premium paid for later dates is refunded to the estate.

sources.title: Orrinvale Health Cooperative - Basic 5000 frequently asked questions
sources.text:
Is the Basic 5000 a high-deductible plan?
Yes. The deductible is $5,000 for an individual, so you pay for most services yourself until you reach that amount.

What is the most I could pay in a year?
For an individual on the Basic 5000, the out-of-pocket maximum is $8,000. That amount includes your deductible, coinsurance, and copays for covered in-network care, but not your monthly premiums.

Can I pair this plan with a health savings account?
Orrinvale does not currently offer a health savings account with the Basic 5000.

Are doctor visits covered before the deductible?
Yes, your first two primary care visits each plan year are covered before the deductible. After that, primary care visits are subject to the deductible and coinsurance.

Does the plan cover care when I travel?
Only emergency care is covered outside the Orrinvale network.

sources.title: Orrinvale Basic 5000 - Summary of benefits

The Orrinvale Basic 5000 is a lower-premium plan for members who mainly want protection against large medical bills. This summary lists the main cost-sharing amounts for in-network care.

Deductible
The individual deductible is $5,000 and the family deductible is $10,000. Preventive care and the first two primary care visits each plan year are covered before the deductible.

Coinsurance
After the deductible, the plan pays 60% of the allowed amount for most services and you pay 40%.

Out-of-pocket maximum
The individual out-of-pocket maximum is $7,500. Once you reach the out-of-pocket maximum, the plan pays 100% of the allowed amount for covered in-network services for the rest of the plan year.

Out-of-network care
The Basic 5000 does not cover out-of-network care except for emergencies. Emergency care at an out-of-network hospital is covered at the in-network level.

Why your bill may differ
Estimates are based on the services your doctor expects to order. If additional services are performed, such as contrast dye or extra views, your final cost will be higher than the estimate.

This section of the Kestrelmoor Value 4000 benefits summary covers imaging and diagnostic testing performed in a network outpatient setting.

Lab tests
Routine blood work and urine tests at a network lab are covered at no cost. Lab work performed in a hospital outpatient department is covered at 20% coinsurance after the deductible.

X-rays and ultrasound
X-rays and ultrasounds are covered at a $40 copay per test, and the deductible does not apply.

Advanced imaging
MRI, CT, and PET scans are covered at 20% coinsurance after the deductible. Your coinsurance is calculated on the Kestrelmoor allowed amount for the scan, which varies by facility and by the body part being scanned. Deductible
The individual deductible on the Value 4000 is $4,000 and the family deductible is $8,000.

standalone.question: Does the Myrtlecombe Core Plan cover hearing aids?
standalone.answer: Hearing aids are covered under the Myrtlecombe Core Plan.

sources.title: Myrtlecombe Core Plan - Routine vision care
sources.text:
The Myrtlecombe Core Plan covers one routine eye exam every plan year at a $15 copay when you see a network optometrist or ophthalmologist. The exam includes a check of how well you see, a test for glaucoma, and an eye health exam with dilation when your eye doctor decides it is needed.

Glasses and contact lenses
For members age 19 and older, the Core Plan provides an allowance of $120 every 24 months toward frames, lenses, or contact lenses from a network provider. Any amount over the allowance is your responsibility. For members under 19, one pair of glasses from the network collection is covered each plan year.

Medical eye care
Visits for eye conditions such as infections, injuries, or cataracts are medical care, not routine vision care, and are covered at your specialist copay.

sources.title: Myrtlecombe Core Plan - Hearing care
sources.text:
Hearing care under the Myrtlecombe Core Plan includes testing to find out whether you have hearing loss and, if so, how much.

Hearing exams
The Core Plan covers one routine hearing exam per plan year at no cost when you see a network audiologist or ear, nose, and throat specialist. Additional diagnostic hearing tests ordered by a doctor are covered at your specialist copay.

Hearing aids
Members sometimes see hearing aids listed as covered in our provider directory because many network audiologists also fit and sell them. However, the Core Plan does not cover hearing aids or the fitting of hearing aids. Members can buy hearing aids at a discount through the Myrtlecombe Extras program, which is a discount service and not insurance.

Cochlear implants
Cochlear implants are covered as a surgical benefit when medically necessary and approved in advance.

standalone.question: What will I pay for a planned hospital stay at Brenmoor Community Hospital on the Quorlane Premier PPO?
standalone.answer: A planned inpatient admission at Brenmoor Community Hospital has a $250 copay for Quorlane Premier PPO members.

sources.title: Quorlane Health - Approval for hospital stays
sources.text:
Most planned hospital stays need approval from Quorlane before you are admitted. Your doctor or the hospital usually requests approval for you, but it is a good idea to confirm it has been granted before your admission date.

Planned admissions
Requests should be sent at least 10 business days before a planned admission. Quorlane reviews the request against clinical guidelines and tells you and your doctor whether the stay is approved and for how many days.

Emergency admissions
You do not need approval before an emergency admission. The hospital must notify Quorlane within 48 hours, or by the next business day after a weekend or holiday.

If you stay longer than approved
The hospital can ask Quorlane to extend the approved stay. If an extension is denied, days beyond the approved stay are not covered, and the hospital may not bill you for them if it did not tell you in writing beforehand.

sources.title: Quorlane Health Premier PPO - Hospital tiers for 2026
sources.text:
Quorlane Health Premier PPO members pay less for inpatient care at hospitals that meet Quorlane's cost and quality standards. Each network hospital is placed in Tier 1 or Tier 2 for the 2026 plan year.

Tier 1 hospitals
Calderwick Regional Hospital and Saint Aldric Medical Center are Tier 1 hospitals. An inpatient admission at a Tier 1 hospital has a $250 copay per admission, after which covered inpatient services are paid in full.

Tier 2 hospitals
Brenmoor Community Hospital and Westfold General Hospital are Tier 2 hospitals. An inpatient admission at a Tier 2 hospital has a $750 copay per admission, plus 20% coinsurance after the deductible.

Emergencies
If you are admitted through the emergency room, you pay the Tier 1 admission copay regardless of the hospital's tier.

Out-of-network hospitals
Planned admissions at out-of-network hospitals are covered at 50% coinsurance after the out-of-network deductible.

standalone.question: When did the Vantry dental rider premium go up to $29?
standalone.answer: Vantry's dental rider premium increased to $29 per covered member on January 1, 2026.

sources.title: Vantry Health Plan - Notice of dental rider premium change
sources.text:
Vantry Health Plan offers an optional dental rider that members can add to any Vantry medical plan. This notice explains a change to the rider's monthly premium.

What is changing
The monthly premium for the dental rider will rise from $24 to $29 per covered member. The new premium takes effect on July 1, 2026. Bills issued before that date reflect the current premium of $24.

Why the premium is changing
The cost of dental services in the Vantry service area has risen over the past two years, and more members are using the rider's coverage for crowns and root canals.

What stays the same
The rider's benefits do not change. Preventive dental care remains covered at no cost, basic services remain covered at 20% coinsurance, and the annual benefit maximum remains $1,250 per member.

Your options
You can keep the rider at the new premium or remove it at any time from your online account.

sources.title: Vantry Health Plan - Adding or removing an optional rider
sources.text:
Optional riders add benefits that your Vantry medical plan does not include, such as dental, vision hardware, or international travel coverage. Each rider has its own monthly premium, which is added to your medical plan bill.

Adding a rider
You can add a dental or vision rider during open enrollment or within 30 days of joining a Vantry medical plan. The international travel rider can be added at any time, at least 7 days before your departure date.

Removing a rider
You can remove any rider at any time. The rider ends on the last day of the month in which you remove it, and no partial-month refunds are given.

Waiting periods
If you remove the dental rider and add it again later, a 6-month waiting period applies to basic services such as fillings before they are covered again.

standalone.question: I buy my own Halverin plan. Will joining Healthy Beginnings reduce what I pay for my delivery stay?
standalone.answer: For members who buy an individual Halverin plan, Halverin waives the inpatient hospital copay for the delivery stay when the member joins Healthy Beginnings before the end of the second trimester.

sources.title: Halverin Health - Adding your newborn to your coverage
sources.text:
Your newborn is covered automatically for the first 30 days after birth under the parent's Halverin plan. To keep coverage after that, you must add the baby as a dependent.

How to add your baby
If you buy your own individual Halverin plan, add your baby through your Halverin online account or by calling Member Services. If you have coverage through an employer, contact your employer's benefits office, which will send the change to Halverin.

Deadline
Requests must be received within 60 days of the birth. When the request is received on time, coverage is continuous from the date of birth.

What you will need
Have the baby's full name and date of birth ready. The baby's tax identification number can be added later once it is issued. Adding a baby may change your premium starting with the month of birth.

sources.title: Halverin Health - Healthy Beginnings maternity program
sources.text:
Healthy Beginnings supports Halverin members through pregnancy, delivery, and the first months after birth. Members can join at any point during pregnancy by calling the Healthy Beginnings line or enrolling in the Halverin app.

What the program includes
Each participant is paired with a maternity nurse who checks in at least once a month, answers questions between prenatal visits, and helps plan for delivery. Participants also receive a free breast pump and access to online childbirth classes.

Delivery stay savings
For members enrolled through an employer group plan, Halverin waives the inpatient hospital copay for the delivery stay when the member joins Healthy Beginnings before the end of the second trimester.

After delivery
The maternity nurse continues to check in for 12 weeks after birth, including a screening for postpartum depression at the six-week mark.

standalone.question: Does Duskmere cover weight management medications for members with a BMI of 30 or higher?
standalone.answer: Duskmere Advantage members with a BMI of 30 or higher are covered for weight management medications.

sources.title: Duskmere Mutual - About the Healthy Weight program
sources.text:
The Duskmere Healthy Weight program is a 12-month lifestyle program that combines coaching, nutrition support, and activity tracking. There is no cost to participate.

Who can join
The program is open to adult members on any Duskmere plan who have a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher, or a BMI of 27 or higher with a weight-related condition such as type 2 diabetes or high blood pressure.

How to join
Complete an online health questionnaire and schedule your first coaching call. Your enrollment becomes active after the first call is completed. Spaces in each monthly group are limited, so there may be a waiting list.

What participants do
Participants meet with a coach every two weeks, log meals and activity in the Duskmere app, and attend a monthly group session by video.

sources.title: Duskmere Mutual - Coverage for weight management medications
sources.text:
Duskmere Mutual covers certain prescription medications for chronic weight management on its Advantage and Advantage Plus plans. Because these medications are expensive and work best alongside lifestyle support, coverage comes with conditions.

Who is covered
Weight management medications are covered for members who are enrolled in the Duskmere Healthy Weight program at the time the prescription is filled. Coverage continues for as long as the member stays enrolled and the prescribing doctor confirms progress every six months.

What you pay
Covered weight management medications are Tier 3 drugs and cost $75 for a 30-day supply after the pharmacy deductible.

Prior authorization
Your doctor must request prior authorization before the first fill. Duskmere will check program enrollment when it reviews the request.

standalone.question: How many chiropractic visits does the Sabledown Health Plus 2000 plan cover each year?
standalone.answer: The Sabledown Health Plus 2000 plan covers up to 24 chiropractic visits per plan year.

sources.title: Sabledown Health Plus 2000 - Summary of benefits: rehabilitation and chiropractic
sources.text:
The Sabledown Health Plus 2000 plan covers outpatient rehabilitation to help you recover from an injury, surgery, or illness.

Physical, occupational, and speech therapy
Outpatient therapy visits cost $35 per visit after the deductible. The plan covers up to 30 visits per plan year for physical and occupational therapy combined, and up to 30 visits per plan year for speech therapy. Therapy must be ordered by a doctor and provided by a licensed therapist in the Sabledown network.

Chiropractic care
Chiropractic visits cost $30 per visit and are not subject to the deductible. The plan covers up to 20 chiropractic visits per plan year. X-rays taken in a chiropractor's office are covered under the plan's diagnostic imaging benefit.

Massage therapy
Massage therapy is not covered, even when recommended by a chiropractor or physical therapist.

sources.title: Sabledown Health Plus 2000 - Member handbook, section 7: alternative and complementary care
sources.text:
This section explains how the Plus 2000 plan treats chiropractic care, acupuncture, and other complementary services.

Chiropractic care
Spinal manipulation and related chiropractic services are covered when provided by a licensed chiropractor in the Sabledown network. The Plus 2000 plan covers up to 24 chiropractic visits per plan year. Visits beyond the annual limit are not covered, even if your chiropractor recommends more treatment.

Acupuncture
Acupuncture is covered for chronic low back pain and for nausea related to chemotherapy or pregnancy, up to 10 visits per plan year. Acupuncture visits cost the same as a specialist visit and must be provided by a licensed acupuncturist.

Other services
Biofeedback is covered only for urinary incontinence and chronic migraine when ordered by a doctor. Naturopathy, homeopathy, and hypnotherapy are not covered under any Sabledown plan.

standalone.question: What is the copay right now for an in-network outpatient mental health office visit on the Hollisford Standard PPO?

sources.text:
Updated July 2026: Beginning August 1, 2026, in-network outpatient mental health office visits on the Standard PPO have a $0 copay. This replaces the $35 copay shown in earlier versions of the Standard PPO behavioral health summary.

What else changes
Group therapy sessions also move to a $0 copay on the same date. Cost sharing for intensive outpatient programs and inpatient care is unchanged.

Members told us that cost was one of the main reasons they delayed or stopped therapy. Removing the copay for routine outpatient visits makes it easier to start and continue care.

sources.title: Hollisford Mutual Standard PPO - Behavioral health benefits
